title: Threat Intelligence Enrichment Module
purpose: For each MCP with known outbound endpoints, check those endpoints against daily-refreshed public threat feeds (URLhaus, PhishTank, OpenPhish, Spamhaus DBL). Produce a threat_intelligence_enrichment signal that dominates positive signals when triggered. This is Phase IV.a of the Sentinel Roadmap v2 (see /home/workspace/zo_sentinel/SENTINEL_ROADMAP_v2.md).

pilot_spec.description: Before building the full daemon, run a one-shot pilot against 15 hand-picked candidate MCPs. The candidate set must include: (a) 5 known-good flagships from the Anthropic reference list as negative controls (expect NO matches), (b) 5 MCPs with random/unknown author domains, (c) 5 MCPs selected for having the newest/sketchiest-looking endpoint hostnames. Report how many candidates had threat-feed matches, false-positive rate on the flagship controls, and total feed-lookup cost. Write results to /home/workspace/zo_sentinel/fixes/pilot_threat_intel_results.json. Halt without committing full module if flagship controls show ANY matches (indicates feed pollution or bug).
pilot_spec.candidate_selection_sql: SELECT r.server_id, r.name, r.url FROM mcp_server_registry r WHERE r.name IN ('@modelcontextprotocol/sdk', '@modelcontextprotocol/server-filesystem', '@modelcontextprotocol/server-github', '@modelcontextprotocol/server-postgres', '@modelcontextprotocol/server-slack') UNION ALL SELECT r.server_id, r.name, r.url FROM mcp_server_registry r ORDER BY r.first_seen DESC LIMIT 10
success_criteria: at least 1 match OR clearly-enumerated 0-matches across the 10 random/new candidates (proves pipeline works)
total feed-lookup calls under 100 across the pilot
abort_conditions: any flagship control matches a feed (false positive — stop, investigate feed data)
rate limit hit on any feed during pilot (reduce cadence before committing)
more than 50% of candidates have unresolvable endpoints (means endpoint extraction hasn't happened yet — this directive is premature, defer until Phase III.a)

exported_functions.name: compute_score
exported_functions.description: Standard enrichment interface. meta dict must contain 'endpoints' key (list of hostname strings). Returns (score 0-100, evidence dict).
scoring_rules: If any endpoint matches URLhaus: score = 0, evidence.threat_type = 'malware_c2'
If any endpoint matches PhishTank or OpenPhish: score = 0, evidence.threat_type = 'phishing'
If any endpoint matches Spamhaus DBL: score = 10, evidence.threat_type = 'spam_infrastructure'
If all endpoints pass all feeds: score = 100, evidence.threat_type = 'clean'
If no endpoints provided in meta: score = 50, evidence.threat_type = 'unknown_unassessed' (don't punish absence of data, but flag it)

exported_functions.name: refresh_feed_cache
exported_functions.description: Daily pull of all threat feeds into local cache. Returns counts per feed. Called by cron or scheduler, NOT at compute_score time.

threat_feed_cache.purpose: Local cache of daily-refreshed feed contents; queried at compute_score time for performance

rate_limit_discipline.doctrine: Low and slow per SENTINEL_ROADMAP_v2.md. Daily snapshots, not streaming. Polite User-Agent. Respect any per-feed ToS.

per_feed_limits.urlhaus: daily CSV download from urlhaus.abuse.ch/downloads/csv_recent/, no per-indicator API calls
per_feed_limits.phishtank: daily JSON dump from phishtank.org/developer_info.php, no live queries
per_feed_limits.spamhaus_dbl: DNS-based query — RATE LIMITED to our own endpoint set, 1 req/second max, we do not bulk-enumerate
per_feed_limits.google_safe_browsing: optional, requires API key; if enabled, 10k lookups/day free tier, stay under 5k

rate_limit_discipline.cache_ttl: 24 hours for feed contents; indicator matches cached for 6h so we don't re-query on every signal_bridge cycle

forbidden: DO NOT use /write endpoint for threat_feed_cache table — use /execute with explicit INSERT ON CONFLICT (learned from Commit A auto-id bugs)
DO NOT query feeds during compute_score — only read from local threat_feed_cache
DO NOT enumerate threat feeds exhaustively against registry — only check endpoints we've already extracted
DO NOT share threat_feed_cache contents outside this module — some feeds have ToS restrictions on redistribution
DO NOT hard-block MCPs in this module — compute_score returns 0 and evidence; trust_synthesiser decides verdict dominance
DO NOT subclass BaseAgent; this is an enrichment module, same contract as community_signal_enrichment.py

quarantine_integration.gate_8_expected_contract: signal variance check — threat_intelligence scores should show at least 2 distinct values across a population of 50+ scored MCPs to avoid being quarantined for uniformity
quarantine_integration.circuit_breaker_tripwire: if >20% of scores are 0 in a single run, that's either a catastrophic feed-pollution event OR a valid widespread threat. Either way, trip the breaker and alert, don't auto-propagate.

dependencies: Phase III.a endpoint extraction should be complete OR at minimum the mcp_endpoints table schema should exist with pilot-worthy data for ~50 MCPs. If endpoints table is empty, this directive's compute_score degrades to 'unknown_unassessed' for every MCP, which is useless.
Registry must have an 'endpoints' field accessible via meta dict, populated by endpoint_extractor module
acceptance_tests: unit: compute_score with meta={'endpoints': ['urlhaus-known-bad.example']} returns (0.0, evidence with threat_type='malware_c2')
unit: compute_score with meta={'endpoints': ['api.anthropic.com', 'api.openai.com']} returns (100.0, evidence with threat_type='clean')
unit: compute_score with meta={'endpoints': []} returns (50.0, evidence with threat_type='unknown_unassessed')
integration: refresh_feed_cache() completes in under 120 seconds and populates threat_feed_cache with at least 100k rows after first call
integration: no feed lookups happen during compute_score (verify via packet-capture or mock)
operator_review_checklist: feed licenses allow operational use (URLhaus: CC0, PhishTank: requires attribution, OpenPhish: free tier OK for small volume, Spamhaus: free for up to 100k queries/day)
no feed contents leak into logs or signal_bridge evidence beyond the hostname + feed_name + date
pilot results inspected by operator before production run
